summary: Scripts can now manage PIM Manager settings and propose changes, Invardia support can fix known problems for you, and one file can set up a new install.

new.title: Manage settings from scripts
new.text: An approved application can change settings and commit changes through the same checks as a person. Turning something on applies at once; switching a protection off waits for a SuperAdmin. Who signs in, approves and acts stays with people.

new.title: Scripts propose, people approve
new.text: An application can propose changes to administrators and their roles. Each proposal waits in Proposals from applications until an Admin or SuperAdmin approves it.

new.title: Invardia support fixes known problems
new.text: When a run fails for a known reason, Invardia support can apply the fix PIM Manager itself offers, on a support ticket, and your admins get a mail. You can choose to approve each fix first.

new.title: One file to set up an install
new.text: A published example script applies a set of settings and permission packs from one file, with a preview first.

fixes.title: Stricter application sign-in
fixes.text: Application tokens must state that they are application tokens and come from your own tenant. Scripts that already use the API need the API setup command run once.
